title: Incorporation of CsPbBr 3  quantum dot into polymer fibers  via  low-polarity co-solvent electrospinning
content: All-inorganic perovskite quantum dots (QDs), such as CsPbBr3, have emerged as promising materials for next-generation light-emitting applications because of their outstanding optical properties. However, their practical use is limited by rapid fluorescence degradation under environmental stressors such as moisture, heat, and ultraviolet irradiation. Incorporating CsPbBr3 QDs into polymer matrices followed by electrospinning can enhance their stability and processability, but the polar co-solvents conventionally required for electrospinning, such as DMF and DMSO, can further compromise QD stability. Here, we show that ethyl acetate and tetrahydrofuran, both of relatively low polarity, serve as effective co-solvents for electrospinning CsPbBr3/poly(methyl methacrylate) (PMMA) and CsPbBr3/polystyrene (PS) mixtures, respectively. The resulting CsPbBr3/PMMA and CsPbBr3/PS mixtures retained 54% and 46% of their initial photoluminescence intensity after 21 days under ambient storage, compared with only 16% for pristine QDs dispersed in toluene alone. Using the same solvent systems, we further fabricated well-defined luminescent CsPbBr3@polymer fibers by electrospinning, with photoluminescence concentrated along the fiber structure. These results establish ethyl acetate and THF as viable low-polarity co-solvents for electrospinning CsPbBr3 QD-incorporated polymer fibers.
